title: Queen's Gambit: traps
line: Two traps: Black holding on to the pawn, and a pawn on d5 that is not free.

steps.text: Black takes the offered pawn and pushes another pawn to hold on to it.
Push the pawn on a2 two squares. It attacks the pawn on b5.
steps.after: Black guards it with one more pawn.

steps.text: Take on b5 to break up Black's chain of pawns.
steps.after: Black takes back. Now no piece stands between f3 and the rook on a8.

steps.text: Bring the queen out on the long diagonal. It attacks the rook on a8.
steps.hint: Your queen can reach the long diagonal that ends at the rook on a8.
steps.after: Any piece that blocks is taken, and if nothing blocks, the rook goes. Holding the pawn cost Black a piece.

steps.text: A trap for White. Black put its other knight on d7. Your bishop pins the knight on f6 to the queen, so it seems unable to move.
Trade pawns on d5. Now only the pinned knight guards the pawn on d5.
Here the knight took the pawn. Black let the queen go, then a bishop check took it back: Black has a piece for a pawn.
Back to the trap. Leave the pawn on d5 alone and move the pawn in front of your king one square.

wrong.c3d5: That is the trap: the knight takes back, and the bishop check wins your queen.

steps.after: White keeps its queen and brings out its pieces.

summary: Holding the gambit pawn with more pawns opens the long diagonal. A knight that looks pinned may still move.
